findings.summary: Answer: no PR code left changes the browser-process lifecycle (error trap, preventDefault, exit requests, control frames) vs main — the trap and handleRealmUncaughtError are main's, so every cancellation form (onerror returning true, prototype preventDefault, several/capture listeners) behaves as main by construction, and main's kernel spec passes. Remaining runtime-owned differences: (a) awaitDrain rejects a non-Error projected reason as itself (main: `new Error(String(v))`) — reached only without an eval projection, changes the rejection value's type for drain consumers (no-COI child prints `String(v)` instead of an Error stack), not exit status; (b) the eval sync catch reshapes a MODULE_NOT_FOUND before dispatch (listeners see the plain Error, as Node); (c) an eval rejection's terminal gets the UnhandledPromiseRejection wrapper; (d) NodeProcessExit.fatal/listenerThrew and the eval terminal print the shared formatter; (e) timer callbacks run as `Timeout#_onTimeout` (`this` = the handle) on every host; (f) runNodeEntry claims/clears the main module.
